# Local Checkouts Bootstrap

XTRM runs from local git checkouts on the operator's machines, not from the npm
registry. Four repositories supply the binaries:

| Checkout | Packages linked globally | Binary |
|---|---|---|
| `core` | `xtrm-tools`, `@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions` | `xt`, `xtrm`, `ghgrep` (from committed `cli/dist`) |
| `xtrm` | `@jaggerxtrm/substrate`, `@xtrm/xtprompt`, `@xtrm/xts` | `sb`, `xtprompt`, `xts` (TypeScript run directly) |
| `xtmux` | `@jaggerxtrm/xtmux` plus `install.sh` | `xtmux`, `tmux-session-picker`, the `tmux` kill guard |
| `specialists` | `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` | `specialists`, `sp` (from committed `dist`) |

`scripts/bootstrap.sh` sets up or updates all four in one run. It needs Node 24 or
later and nothing else — it runs before `xt` exists on the machine.

## What it does

An apply run (no `--check`) performs three phases.

1. **Git phase, per repository.**
   - A missing checkout is cloned from its remote.
   - An existing checkout is fetched (`git fetch --prune origin`) and fast-forwarded
     to the remote default branch with `git merge --ff-only` when it is clean and
     behind.
   - The script stops for that repository, and reports it, when the checkout is
     dirty (tracked modifications or staged changes), diverged, ahead of the remote,
     on another branch, on a detached HEAD, or when the fetch fails. It never
     force-resets and never discards work.
   - Untracked files are listed as information and do not block the update.
2. **Install phase, per repository that is clean after phase 1.**
   - For each linked package directory the script runs the dependency install with
     the package manager the repository pins: `bun install --frozen-lockfile` when
     only `bun.lock` exists and `bun` is on `PATH`; `npm install` when
     `package-lock.json` exists; otherwise `npm install --no-package-lock` so a run
     never creates a new lockfile.
   - It then runs `npm link` in that directory, which registers the package and its
     bins in the global npm prefix.
   - For `xtmux` it also runs the repository installer (`install.sh`), which places
     the bins and the `tmux` kill guard in `~/.local/bin`, installs the Pi package
     copy, the Claude and Codex hooks, and writes
     `~/.local/state/xtmux/installer.json`.
3. **Report.** The script prints the checkouts (branch, commit, package version,
   state), every binary with the path it resolves to and the checkout, commit and
   version behind it, the xtmux installer state, and a drift and problem list.

## Usage

```bash
# from the core checkout, on any machine
./scripts/bootstrap.sh --check     # read-only: report drift, change nothing
./scripts/bootstrap.sh             # clone/fast-forward, install, link, report
./scripts/bootstrap.sh --json      # machine-readable report
```

The script fetches in both modes: `--check` needs `origin` to compare against.
It writes nothing to the checkouts or to the home directory in `--check` mode.

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--check` | Report drift only. No clone, pull, install, link or installer run. |
| `--root <dir>` | Directory that holds the checkouts. Default `~/dev`. |
| `--json` | Print the report as JSON. |
| `--no-install` | Git phase only; skip dependency install, `npm link` and the installer. |
| `--no-links` | Skip link creation, link verification and the xtmux installer. |
| `-h`, `--help` | Print usage. |

| Environment variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `XTRM_BOOTSTRAP_REPOS_JSON` | Replace the built-in repository table (name, directory, remote, linked package directories, optional installer). Use it for a non-standard layout, or in tests. |
| `XTRM_BOOTSTRAP_NPM` | npm executable to use instead of the one resolved from `PATH`. |
| `npm_config_prefix` | Honoured by `npm link` and by link verification, so a run can target a prefix other than the machine default. |

Exit codes: `0` nothing to do or everything succeeded, `1` drift found or a step
failed, `2` usage error.

## Report

```text
XTRM local checkouts — check (read-only)
  root: ~/dev
  npm:  /home/dawid/.nvm/versions/node/v25.2.1/bin/npm

checkouts
  repo         branch  commit    state
  core         main    21347c6b  ok
  xtrm         main    28657ffd  behind
  xtmux        main    c8a74384  ok
  specialists  master  c17901a9  ok

links
  binary               resolves to                                 state  note
  xt                   ~/dev/core/cli/dist/index.cjs               ok
  sb                   ~/dev/xtrm/packages/substrate/cli/sb-ux.ts  ok
  tmux                 ~/dev/xtmux/bin/tmux-guard                  ok
  ...

drift (2)
  - xtrm: 8 commit(s) behind origin/main
  - xtmux: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json loads xtmux from the checkout directly ...
```

Each link row names the resolved path, the owning repository and commit, and the
package version. A row whose resolved path is outside the owning checkout is a
`mismatch`: another install shadows the checkout. A `missing` row means no link
exists. A `note` marks a binary shadowed earlier on `PATH` (for example
`/usr/bin/tmux` in front of the `~/.local/bin/tmux` guard).

## Safety rules

- Uncommitted work is never discarded. A dirty checkout stops the update for that
  repository and is reported. Nothing runs `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`
  or `git clean`.
- No `tmux kill-server`, no restarts of running agents, no changes to a running
  tmux server. The xtmux installer is called without `--tmux-hooks`.
- Every step is idempotent: a second run on a clean machine reports no drift and
  changes nothing.
- `--check` never mutates state. Only the network `fetch` runs.

## A new machine

Prerequisites: `git`, `node` 24 or later, `npm`, `ssh` access to the four remotes,
and `bun` (used by the `specialists` and `xtmux` dependency installs).

```bash
git clone git@github.com:xtrm-dev/core.git ~/dev/core
~/dev/core/scripts/bootstrap.sh            # clones the other three, installs, links
~/dev/core/scripts/bootstrap.sh --check    # expect: no drift
```

Then confirm the binaries and the guard:

```bash
xt --version && sb --help >/dev/null && sp --version
xtmux --version
command -v tmux    # must print ~/.local/bin/tmux, the kill guard
```

`~/.local/bin` must precede the system paths on `PATH` so the `tmux` guard wins.

## The server over ssh

The same script runs on the server from its own `core` checkout:

```bash
ssh <server> '~/dev/core/scripts/bootstrap.sh --check'
ssh <server> '~/dev/core/scripts/bootstrap.sh'
```

`--json` gives a report that a local script can diff between machines. The script
requires no interactive input, so it is safe over a non-interactive ssh command.

## Troubleshooting

| Report | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `dirty` | The checkout has tracked modifications or staged changes. | Commit, stash or revert them deliberately, then re-run. The script does not touch them. |
| `diverged` | Local commits and remote commits both exist. | Rebase or merge by hand, then re-run. |
| `ahead` | Local commits are not pushed. | Push them, or accept that the checkout is intentionally ahead. |
| `wrong-branch` | The checkout is on another branch. | `git switch <default>` when the branch is finished; the script never switches. |
| `detached` | The checkout is on a detached HEAD. | `git switch <default>`. |
| `installer-missing` | No `~/.local/state/xtmux/installer.json`. | Run the apply mode so `install.sh` runs. |
| `installer-root` | The installer state points at another checkout. | Re-run the apply mode from the checkout that should own the bins. |
| `installer-version` | Installed xtmux version differs from the checkout. | Re-run the apply mode. |
| `installer-payload` | A directory the installer recorded (Pi package copy, Claude or Codex hooks) is gone. | Re-run the apply mode. |
| `fetch-failed` | `git fetch` failed, so drift cannot be judged. | Fix the remote access (ssh key, network), then re-run. |
| `pi-entry-conflict` | `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` loads xtmux from the checkout as a source-form entry, so the installer would register a second grouped copy. | Resolve the duplicate entry by hand; the script skips the installer until it is gone. |
| `link-missing`, `link-mismatch` | A binary is absent or resolves outside its checkout. | Re-run the apply mode; a mismatch usually means a stale global install shadows the link. |
| `npm install failed` / `npm link failed` | A dependency or link step failed. | Read the printed tail; fix the environment (network, prefix permissions), then re-run. |

## Why this is not `xt bootstrap`

`xt bootstrap` is a deprecated command that populates the global skills payload for
an already installed CLI. It cannot set up a machine that has no `xt` yet, and it
does not manage checkouts or links. `xt update` reconciles the `.xtrm` payload inside
a repository; `xt doctor` audits runtime settings. None of them clones, fast-forwards
or links the four checkouts, so this script is separate and shell-invoked.

## Tests

`scripts/__tests__/bootstrap.test.mjs` covers the git states (clean, dirty, behind,
missing, diverged, untracked, wrong branch), the install and link path against a
temporary npm prefix, and the Pi entry conflict. It builds throwaway origin
repositories in a temporary directory and needs no network access.

```bash
npm run test:scripts
```
